compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Reconcile planning currently mixes snapshot reads, binding lifecycle decisions, global mode caps, and later handler assumptions. Preview exposes mutations but not the lifecycle effects a live pass would attempt. Without a pure plan value, retry recovery can recompute against different observations and global filters can be applied after decision-bearing work.

## Outcome
Build one immutable observation per pass and pure `TicketPlan` values per local/remote identity. A plan contains the existing `Mutation` values plus lifecycle intents, ticket dependencies, diagnostics, disposition, and observation/version identity. Run selection, filter, mode cap, and global safety limits before any lifecycle or remote effect. Emit the new plan in shadow while legacy dispatch remains authoritative.

## Plan
1. Define immutable observation and plan value objects using open provider-neutral payloads. Keep the existing `Mutation` vocabulary/serialization unchanged.
2. Refactor existing differ outputs into a pure planner that consumes local snapshot, remote snapshot, binding read view, mode, selection/filter, and caps without I/O.
3. Represent bind/confirm/re-key/retire/baseline/comment identity changes as versioned lifecycle intents; do not execute them during planning.
4. Encode inter-ticket dependencies such as create-before-link and parent-before-child explicitly in plans. A blocked prerequisite yields a deferred disposition rather than an out-of-order mutation.
5. Extend dry-run/check preview with a versioned lifecycle-intents section while preserving the existing mutation array shape and hashes. Shadow-compare plan mutations/dispositions to legacy output and fail loudly on unexplained divergence in tests.

## Testing (RED → GREEN)
- Pure table tests feed frozen local/remote/binding snapshots and assert exact plans, dependencies, diagnostics, and dispositions with no patched filesystem/provider calls.
- Ordering tests prove selection/filter/caps happen before lifecycle intent and that truncated scope cannot mutate or advance unselected tickets.
- Preview golden tests preserve legacy mutation bytes/hash and add a versioned lifecycle-intent section.
- Ticket-sourced cases cover tombstones, pending/index lag, moved keys, hierarchy/link ordering, impossible links, partial snapshots, and filtered passes.

## Compatibility / rollback
Shadow mode has zero write authority. Removing the shadow planner returns to legacy differ/preview unchanged. Existing mutation fields and stored ticket/binding formats remain readable; consumers can ignore the additive versioned lifecycle-intent section. No adapter call or binding save is permitted from the planner.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Given the same frozen observation, planning is deterministic and produces immutable per-ticket mutations, lifecycle intents, dependencies, diagnostics, disposition, and version identity with zero I/O.
- [ ] Selection, filter, mode cap, and global safety limits exclude work before any lifecycle intent or remote operation is eligible.
- [ ] Create/link and hierarchy prerequisites are explicit; blocked work is deferred and never emitted out of order.
- [ ] Preview preserves the existing mutation array and canonical hash while adding a versioned lifecycle-intents section that old consumers may ignore.
- [ ] Shadow comparisons match existing provider-neutral mutation/disposition behavior for ticket-sourced regressions or name each approved behavioral delta.
- [ ] Construction, check, dry-run, and shadow planning perform zero repository saves, ticket writes, Jira calls, or child-process launches.
